cards.explanation: The answer is "my beloved child." Paul opens with "To Timothy, my beloved child…" (2 Timothy 1:2). Before he asks for anything or teaches anything, he says how much Timothy means to him. A letter that starts with love gets read twice.
The answer is True. Paul says, "…as I constantly remember you night and day in my prayers." (2 Timothy 1:3). Night AND day, friends. I think that's what being loved looks like.

The answer is True. Paul writes, "Recalling your tears, I long to see you so that I may be filled with joy." (2 Timothy 1:4). He remembers Timothy's tears and he misses him. Seeing Timothy is what he says would fill him with joy.

The answer is Lois and Eunice. Paul says the faith "…first dwelt in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice…" (2 Timothy 1:5). Lois is the grandmother and Eunice is the mother. It lived in them first, and Paul is convinced it's in Timothy as well.
The answer is to fan it into flame. Paul says, "…fan into flame the gift of God, which is in you…" (2 Timothy 1:6). You fan a fire to make it burn bright. Don't let it sit there and sulk, friends.

The word is "fear." "For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control." (2 Timothy 1:7). A spirit of fear isn't what God has given us. Power, love and self-control are, and that's a much better bag of gifts.
The first thing Paul names is the testimony of our Lord. He says, "So do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord…" (2 Timothy 1:8). Then he adds a second thing, so keep reading, bakers.
The answer is True. Paul writes, "…or of me, His prisoner." (2 Timothy 1:8). He's in chains, and he calls himself the Lord's prisoner. I think that tells you whose prisoner he feels he really is.

The answer is False. Paul says, "…join me in suffering for the gospel by the power of God." (2 Timothy 1:8). The strength comes from God, not from Timothy's own muscles. That's good news, friends, because my own muscles are just a mustache.

The answer is His own purpose and grace. Paul says God saved us and called us "…not because of our works, but by His own purpose and by the grace He granted us in Christ Jesus…" (2 Timothy 1:9). It's all on God's side, friends. His purpose and His grace are what's behind it.
The answer is True. God's grace was granted to us "…in Christ Jesus before time began." (2 Timothy 1:9). Before time began, friends. That grace was there before the first clock ever ticked.

The word is "death." Christ Jesus "…has abolished death and illuminated the way to life and immortality through the gospel…" (2 Timothy 1:10). Abolished. That's not a small word. I'd put it on a banner.

The answer is False. Paul writes, "…even though I suffer as I do, I am not ashamed…" (2 Timothy 1:12). He's honest about the suffering, and he's just as honest that he isn't ashamed. Both are true at once.

The answer is that he knows whom he has believed. Paul says, "for I know whom I have believed, and I am convinced that He is able to guard what I have entrusted to Him for that day." (2 Timothy 1:12). His reason isn't a circumstance, friends. It's a Person he knows.

The answer is the Holy Spirit who dwells in us. Paul says, "Guard the treasure entrusted to you, with the help of the Holy Spirit who dwells in us." (2 Timothy 1:14). Timothy isn't guarding it alone. The Spirit is helping him.

The reason is that he often refreshed Paul and wasn't ashamed of Paul's chains. Paul writes, "…because he has often refreshed me and was unashamed of my chains." (2 Timothy 1:16). Paul had told Timothy not to be ashamed of him, and here is Onesiphorus, who wasn't.
The word is "searched." "…when he arrived in Rome, he searched diligently until he found me." (2 Timothy 1:17). Diligently means he kept at it, friends. He didn't stop until he found Paul.

The answer is True. Paul says, "You know very well how much he ministered to me in Ephesus." (2 Timothy 1:18). He's speaking to Timothy there. Paul is reminding him of something Timothy knows very well.
